data.name: Dattatray
data.long_meaning: Dattatray is a name derived from the Sanskrit words ‘Datta’ (given) and ‘Tray’ (God). This name is given to those who believe in the power of the gods and seek their guidance in life. In Hindu mythology, Dattatray is the name of Lord Dattatreya, a deity who is revered as the embodiment of three gods – Lord Brahma, Lord Vishnu, and Lord Shiva.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dattatray is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and demonstrates the importance of divinity in Hindu culture. By giving a child this name, the parents are passing on the values and beliefs of their ancestors, imbuing the child with a sense of connection to their heritage and tradition. Dattatray represents the belief that the gods are always present and actively involved in the lives of their devotees, guiding them towards the right path. The name carries with it a rich cultural legacy, inspiring a deep sense of pride and belonging.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Dattatray holds significant spiritual significance as it symbolizes surrender to the divine will. Lord Dattatreya, the embodiment of the three gods, is venerated as a provider of immense knowledge and grace. By invoking the name of this deity, one seeks his blessings and guidance in matters of the soul. This name encourages humility, self-reflection, and a deep sense of devotion towards the divine, inspiring one to lead a virtuous and righteous life. The name Dattatray is a constant reminder of the importance of surrendering oneself to the will of the divine, and seeking their guidance and blessings in all matters of life.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Lord Dattatraya is an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. He appeared in the form of a sage to test the devotion of King Yuddhajit.
historical_references.context: During the Mahabharata era, King Yuddhajit was infamous for his cruelty towards sages and ascetics. Lord Vishnu, in order to test the king's devotion, appeared in the form of the sage Dattatraya and lived in his kingdom as an ascetic. The king, unaware of Dattatraya's true identity, mistreated him. Dattatraya, in order to test the king's devotion, asked for three boons. The king granted them, but in the process, he insulted Dattatraya, thereby violating the terms of the boons. As a result, the king was cursed and died a miserable death.

historical_references.reference: Lord Dattatraya is also known as 'Trimurti' because he embodies the three primary deities - Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva.
historical_references.context: The concept of Lord Dattatraya as the embodiment of the Trimurti is a deep philosophical belief in Hinduism. It signifies the unity in diversity and the interconnectedness of all deities in the Hindu pantheon. This belief is not tied to a specific historical period or event but is an integral part of Hindu mythology and philosophy.
